title: 01 — Commercial performance
text: Atlas is a commercial intelligence workbench built around a reproducible synthetic pharmaceutical portfolio. These are fictional sales, not company records. The dashboard covers four Gulf markets, eight products, and forty eight months. In this reporting period, revenue reached seventeen point four million dollars, but attainment remained below plan. Kuwait is the market to review. The purpose is to prioritize a business conversation, not to infer a cause from a chart.

title: 02 — Inspect the evidence
text: The investigation workspace connects a question to numerical evidence. A LangGraph workflow resolves the reporting scope, compiles the metric definition, validates the SQL, and queries PostgreSQL through a restricted role. Users can inspect the query, give feedback, and follow up in context. This demonstration uses the deterministic guided planner. Unsupported product filters and reporting periods ask for clarification instead of silently returning broader totals. The optional live model integration is a separate, unevaluated mode.

title: 03 — Compare against a baseline
text: The outlook compares exponential smoothing with a seasonal naive baseline. On the six month synthetic test window, the selected model has one point two five percent mean absolute percentage error, versus four point seven percent for the baseline. Model selection uses an earlier validation window. Future intervals are exploratory. A sales drop is a signal to investigate, not proof of causation. The promotion experiment demonstrates randomized statistical testing on simulated data, not real pharmaceutical effectiveness.

title: 04 — Support the review
text: Saved briefs summarize revenue, target attainment, the largest product gaps, and a proposed next check. They remain drafts for human review. PostgreSQL supplies the same metric definitions to the interface, agent, and business intelligence export. Thirty backend tests and sixty guided regression cases pass. Those results are not live language model accuracy. Cloud deployment and remote traces remain separate release work. Atlas demonstrates a traceable route from a commercial question to evidence and a decision conversation.
